AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic disease characterized by infiltration of eosinophils in the esophageal epithelium. There are limited treatment options for EoE.

AbstractText.Label: RATIONALE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the long term safety and efficacy of reslizumab (RSZ) in pediatric patients who received RSZ in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) and expanded access program.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Records of patients who received RSZ in our center were reviewed. Patients received RSZ 2 mg/kg (or placebo) every 4 weeks as part of the RCT, open label extension (OLE), and compassionate use (CU). Data were analyzed as of their most recent evaluation in August 2017. Labwork, history, and examinations were conducted every 12 weeks. Biopsy results were compared from baseline (prior to RCT) and at the most recent evaluation. Adverse events (AE) were recorded.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 12 patients entered the RCT at our center. 6 patients completed the OLE. 4 received RSZ through CU. Between the RCT, OLE, and CU periods, patients received 549 doses of RSZ (median 37, range 2-116). No serious AE were attributed to RSZ. Symptoms improved on treatment: dysphagia (42% vs 0%); abdominal pain (58% vs 0%); heartburn (18% vs. 0%); vomiting (67% vs. 17%); reflux (58% vs. 0%). Median esophageal eosinophil count improved (35 eos/hpf vs 3, p value < 0.001). Patients receiving reslizumab maintain a relatively unrestricted diet.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Reslizumab appears to be safe in children with eosinophilic esophagitis over 9 years of treatment experience. Symptoms and eosinophil count improved considerably during treatment with reslizumab despite a relatively unrestricted diet.
